issues.description: Switching the FIFO fd to blocking mode and then read()-ing without bound can deadlock the parent
issues.detail: Once the writer subprocess sends one byte and then misbehaves — hangs after writing, fails to close its end of the FIFO, forks a child that inherits the write end, or simply takes a long time between chunks — the parent enters an unbounded blocking read() loop with no select.poll(), no timeout, and no check_process_exited() guard. The original code preserved liveness by polling on every iteration; the patch trades a real correctness bug (truncation) for a real liveness bug (indefinite hang) and does not state which it prefers. The postcondition 'function returns the complete payload OR signals failure in bounded time' is no longer established.

issues.description: Author cannot state the loop invariant of the outer while after the patch
issues.detail: The outer loop now has two exits — the inner 'break' after draining, and the fall-through if no data ever arrives — but the BlockingIOError branch and the empty-events branch have both been reduced to 'pass'. The invariant 'either content == bytes-read-so-far AND writer-still-open, OR we are about to return' is no longer maintained: on a spurious wakeup with zero events and zero data, the loop now spins without progress and without termination function. There is no decreasing measure. This is UNREASONED control flow.

issues.description: fcntl mode-switch is not exception-safe and leaves the fd in blocking state on error
issues.detail: F_SETFL is called immediately after the first successful read, but the function has no try/finally restoring O_NONBLOCK on the way out. If the subsequent blocking read raises (signal, OSError), or the caller reuses fifo_fd, the descriptor's flags are permanently mutated as a side effect of this function. The frame condition 'fifo_fd's flags are unchanged on exit' is violated silently. A reasoned implementation states the frame and restores it.

issues.description: Diagnosis treats the POSIX guarantee as sufficient without stating the precondition it depends on
issues.detail: The PR text asserts: 'blocking read() returns EOF ONLY after writer closes AND all kernel pipe buffers are drained.' True — but only if exactly one writer ever held the write end and it has closed. FIFOs can have multiple writers; subprocess fork/exec can leak the write fd to grandchildren; on some platforms a re-opener can re-attach. The fix is correct only under a precondition the patch does not state and the surrounding code does not enforce. TESTED-NOT-PROVED: the author has reproduced the truncation and patched the symptom, not reasoned about the writer-set.

issues.description: SMUGGLED-GOTO: the inner 'break' after the blocking drain is a goto out of two loops
issues.detail: The new structure is: outer while; inside it a successful read triggers a mode change, an inner while True, and then an unconditional break of the outer. This is precisely the unstructured exit Dijkstra warned about — a flag-free goto whose target is 'leave the function, but only after the inner loop terminates by a different mechanism.' A structured rewrite states the postcondition once and exits once: read until EOF, return content. The two-phase nonblocking-then-blocking dance should be extracted into a named procedure with a stated specification, not stitched into the existing loop.

issues.description: Removal of check_process_exited() empty-events branch is unjustified
issues.detail: The deleted code handled a real case: writer has exited, poll returned no events, read returned no data, and we already have content — return it. The patch deletes this branch without argument, on the assumption that we will never reach it because we always switch to blocking mode after the first read. That assumption holds only if the first poll() that fires also yields a non-empty read. Under load with EAGAIN on the first read (the BlockingIOError branch, which the patch reduces to 'pass'), control returns to the top of the outer loop in non-blocking mode forever — content is still empty, mode is never switched, and the deleted exit condition is the one that would have saved us. The deletion is not safe.

issues.description: No test exercises the race the patch claims to fix
issues.detail: The PR cites an intermittent JSONDecodeError at ~86KB and claims POSIX semantics resolve it. There is no test in the diff that constructs a writer which writes >PIPE_BUF, closes, and exits between the parent's poll and read — the precise interleaving the patch addresses. 'Testing shows the presence of bugs, not their absence' — but here we have neither a proof nor a test. The change should not land without at least one deterministic regression test exercising the writer-exits-with-buffered-data interleaving.

issues.description: Magic 8192 read size repeated without justification
issues.detail: Both the non-blocking and the new blocking read use 8192. Neither is documented; neither is tied to PIPE_BUF or to a pageable boundary. A reasoned implementation either names the constant (CHUNK_BYTES) and states why, or reads PIPE_BUF and explains the choice. Minor, but symptomatic of code-by-folklore.

issues.description: Comment 'POSIX guaranteed' is a thought-terminator, not a proof
issues.detail: The comment 'this is POSIX guaranteed' substitutes invocation of authority for reasoning. State the actual guarantee: 'For a FIFO with exactly one writer that has close(2)d its only write fd, a blocking read(2) on the read end returns 0 iff the pipe buffer is empty.' Then the reader of this code can check whether the precondition holds. As written, the comment defers the reasoning rather than performing it.

review.summary: Verdict: TESTED-NOT-PROVED, with SMUGGLED-GOTO and DEFENSIVE-AS-SUBSTITUTE. The patch correctly diagnoses a real race — the parent's non-blocking reader can declare EOF while kernel pipe buffers still hold writer bytes — and the POSIX semantics it appeals to are real. But it trades a truncation bug for a hang bug: once switched to blocking mode the parent has no timeout, no poll, no liveness check, and no exception-safe restoration of the fd's flags. The author cannot state the loop invariant or the termination function for the resulting two-phase loop, and the deletion of the check_process_exited() empty-events exit removes the very escape hatch that protected the BlockingIOError path. What would have to change: state the precondition (single writer, no fd leakage); preserve the poll-based liveness check inside the blocking phase (or use a deadline); make the F_SETFL change exception-safe; restore or replace the deleted process-exit guard; and add a deterministic regression test for the writer-exits-with-buffered-data interleaving. REFUSED in present form.
